events.headline: Trump Rejects Iran's Qatar-Mediated Plan to Reopen Strait of Hormuz
events.summary: Iran's foreign minister Araghchi said Tehran offered, via Qatar, a seven-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume nuclear talks in exchange for the US lifting its naval blockade, waiving oil sanctions, and extending the ceasefire to Lebanon. Trump rejected the proposal as 'not acceptable,' saying Iran is 'losing badly.'

events.headline: DRC Ebola Deaths Climb to 4,242 in History's Deadliest Outbreak
events.summary: A WHO Disease Outbreak News update reported 8,787 confirmed cases and 4,242 deaths in the DRC's Ebola outbreak as of Oct 7, 2026, a case fatality rate of 48.3%, up from 8,728 cases and 4,205 deaths the day before. Including cases in Kenya and Uganda, the regional toll is about 4,245, making it the largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded in DRC.

events.headline: Houthi Strike on Riyadh Airport Kills 12 in Deadliest Attack in a Decade
events.summary: An Oct 10 Houthi strike on Riyadh's King Khalid airport killed 12 people, including Saudi, Bangladeshi, US, Jordanian, Palestinian, Syrian, Sudanese and Egyptian nationals, and wounded more than 300. It was the third Houthi strike on the airport in a week and the deadliest attack on Saudi Arabia in a decade.

events.headline: Spain's Sánchez Calls Snap Election After Madrid Eviction Death Protests
events.summary: About 20,000 people marched in Madrid on Oct 8-9 mourning Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old evicted pensioner who died weeks later, after Congress rejected Sánchez's housing-relief decrees on Oct 2. Sánchez subsequently dissolved parliament and called a snap general election for Nov 29, 2026.

events.headline: Hurricane Simón Strengthens to Category 4, Nears Jalisco Landfall
events.summary: Hurricane Simón intensified to Category 4 with winds near 145-150 mph by Oct 10, with forecasters expecting landfall near La Huerta-Tomatlán, Jalisco, on the morning of Oct 11. Mexican authorities suspended classes in 22 coastal municipalities and began evacuations ahead of forecast 10-30 inches of rain and life-threatening storm surge.

events.headline: Russian Guided-Bomb Strike on Zaporizhzhia Apartment Block Kills 20
events.summary: A Russian strike using guided aerial bombs hit a five-storey residential building in Zaporizhzhia on the morning of Oct 10, damaging more than 26 buildings across two districts. The death toll rose through the day to 20, including three children, with about 18 more people injured.

events.headline: Ethiopia, Eritrea Accuse Each Other of Launching War Over Tigray
events.summary: Ethiopia accused Eritrea of an 'all-out invasion' and demanded a troop withdrawal, while Eritrea said it faced a 'war of aggression,' with Eritrean soldiers reported in and around Adigrat, Tigray. The escalation follows an Oct 4 summit in Alamein where Egypt, Eritrea, Sudan and Somalia formed a joint front against Ethiopia.

events.headline: UN Report Names Political, Economic Figures Backing Haiti's Gangs Ahead of First Elections in a Decade
events.summary: A new United Nations report identified specific political and economic figures accused of financing and protecting Haiti's armed gangs, as the country prepares for its first elections in a decade amid continued gang expansion. The findings add pressure on authorities already struggling to contain escalating violence in Port-au-Prince.

events.headline: Saudi Coalition Destroys 82 Houthi Targets as Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Pakistan Activate Mecca Defense Pact
events.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed 82 Houthi targets in "Operation Dawn of Yemen," while Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan activated the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, a new multinational military pact. The moves mark a major escalation and expansion of the military alliance confronting Houthi forces in Yemen.

events.headline: Drone Strike on Sudan Displacement Camp Raises Blue Nile Toll to 41
events.summary: An Oct 9 drone strike near the Abu Shandi camp in Wad al-Mahi, Blue Nile state, killed mostly women and children; the UN says at least 40 died while a rights group puts the toll at 41, with dozens more hospitalized and the number expected to rise. The Rapid Support Forces have been blamed for the attack.
events.locationName: Wad al-Mahi, Blue Nile State, Sudan

events.headline: India Detains Over 2,000 Protesters in Delhi Crackdown Before Election Rally
events.summary: Police detained more than 2,000 people, including 'Cockroach Janta Party' founder Abhijeet Dipke, opposition MPs, journalists and former chief ministers, to quash an Oct 10 rally in New Delhi demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over a voter-roll revision dropping about 130 million names. More than 45 metro stations closed and over 240 trains were cancelled.

events.headline: Panama Declares Emergency After M7.7 Quake Damages 400+ Buildings
events.summary: The M7.7 earthquake that struck southern Panama near the Herrera/Coclé area on Oct 9 triggered regional tsunami warnings across Latin America that were later lifted. No deaths were reported, but 16-27 people were injured and more than 400 homes and buildings, including a hotel and church, were damaged, prompting a state of emergency on Oct 10.

events.headline: Rights Groups Mark Gaza Ceasefire Anniversary, Cite Ongoing Strikes
events.summary: More than 100 rights organizations say the US-backed Gaza ceasefire, in effect since Oct 10, 2025, exists only on paper, citing 1,400-1,481 Palestinians killed and about 5,000 wounded since the truce, plus more than 5,100 reported Israeli violations. Israeli strikes continued into the anniversary on Oct 10, killing several more Palestinians including a child.

events.headline: Trump Says Ukraine Needs 'New President' After Diesel-Deal Clash
events.summary: On Oct 10, Trump said Ukraine 'needs a new president,' blaming President Zelenskyy's refinery strikes for rising diesel prices, after Zelenskyy condemned a new US-Russia diesel export deal. The sharp public rupture comes weeks after Trump signed a Russia sanctions law.

events.headline: Hurricane Isaias Makes Landfall as Category 2 Storm on US Gulf Coast
events.summary: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near the Alabama-Florida border as a Category 2 storm on October 8-9, prompting multi-state emergency declarations and evacuations along the Gulf Coast. Authorities warned of storm surge, flooding and wind damage across coastal Alabama and the Florida Panhandle.

events.headline: Trump-Putin Diesel Deal Waives Russia Sanctions Through April 2027
events.summary: Putin agreed on Oct 9 to supply global diesel markets, including up to 3 million tons of exports, to help lower US fuel prices ahead of the midterms, and the US Treasury issued a temporary license permitting sale, delivery and import of Russian diesel through April 7, 2027. Senate Democrats and Zelenskyy criticized the arrangement.

events.headline: New York Measles Emergency: 108 Cases Confirmed as Disaster Order Runs Through Nov 4
events.summary: New York Governor Hochul's statewide measles disaster emergency, effective Oct 5 through Nov 4, covers 108 confirmed cases as of Oct 3, including 92 since mid-July. The outbreak is concentrated in under-immunized rural counties.

events.headline: Brazil's Lula Government Extends $1.5 Billion Fuel Subsidy Ahead of Oct 25 Runoff
events.summary: Brazil's government opened an extraordinary credit line of roughly $1.51 billion on Oct 8 to extend fuel price subsidies as Lula faces Flávio Bolsonaro in an Oct 25 presidential runoff. The move comes amid persistent inflation pressure and a tight race between the two candidates.

events.headline: Russia Denies Second Plague-Linked Case as WHO Presses Irkutsk Lab
events.summary: Following the Oct 2 death of researcher Darya Shipilova, WHO's Tedros urged Russia to clarify reports of a second employee at an Irkutsk plague institute with unexplained pneumonia. Russia's health watchdog dismissed the reports as 'false information' and said it found no evidence of plague, while the US reportedly sent a formal démarche.

events.headline: China, EU Reach Deal to Curb Hybrid-Car Exports, Ease Rare-Earth Rules
events.summary: After Oct 8-9 talks in Beijing between the EU's Šefčovič and China's Wang Wentao, the two sides reached an understanding to roughly halve China's projected hybrid and plug-in hybrid exports to Europe. China will lower tariffs on about 4 billion euros of EU goods and ease rare-earth and magnet export licensing via a 'green channel,' with follow-up talks planned for January and March.

events.headline: Indonesia Accepts Singapore, Malaysia Aid to Fight Haze-Causing Fires
events.summary: Indonesia confirmed it welcomes assistance from Singapore and Malaysia to combat forest fires in Sumatra and Borneo, with Malaysia committing aircraft, three helicopters and 52 personnel. Haze continues over Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore with unhealthy air quality readings ahead of the Singapore F1 weekend.

events.headline: Ukraine Expands Drone Campaign, Claims Over Half of Russia's Refining Capacity Knocked Out
events.summary: Ukraine's drone campaign against Russian energy infrastructure expanded Oct 8-9 to hit a missile-fuel-component factory in Tver Oblast, facilities in Nizhny Novgorod, and Lukoil's Ukhta refinery — the fourth Russian refinery struck that week after Omsk. Kyiv claims cumulative strikes have knocked out more than half of Russia's oil refining capacity.

events.headline: Sinaloa Prison Riot Death Toll Confirmed at 10, Including a Visitor
events.summary: A riot at the Mazatlán penitentiary in Sinaloa on Oct 8 during family visiting hours left nine inmates and one visitor dead and 16 injured. State and federal forces were deployed; the cause and the method by which any weapons were obtained remain undisclosed.

events.headline: Netanyahu's Ex-Chief of Staff Accused of Altering Oct 7 Call Timestamp
events.summary: Netanyahu's former military secretary Avi Gil alleges that ex-chief of staff Tzachi Braverman instructed a stenographer to change the recorded time of Netanyahu's first Oct 7, 2023 phone call from 6:40am to 6:29am, and allegedly altered it by hand after the stenographer refused. Police reportedly have evidence to indict for record tampering but are unlikely to file charges.

events.headline: US Marine Arrested for Murder of Japanese Woman in Okinawa, Sparking Diplomatic Protest
events.summary: US Marine Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, was arrested Oct 3, 2026 for the murder of 39-year-old Anna Yagi in Naha, Okinawa, allegedly after robbing her at a hotel. Japan lodged a formal protest and US forces imposed a 30-day curfew and 48-hour alcohol ban on personnel.

events.headline: South Africa Anti-Migrant Violence Escalates: Dozens of Vehicles Torched in Durban and Soweto
events.summary: Anti-migrant violence intensified Oct 8-9 in South Africa, with at least 14 vehicles burned in Durban and 10 in Soweto, alongside looting of migrant-run stores. The US Consulate General in Durban closed on Oct 9 citing a security alert.

events.headline: Nigeria Bandit Attack on Zamfara Military Base, Mining Site Kills Dozens
events.summary: An Oct 5 bandit attack on a military base in Bindin, Maru local government area, killed at least 25 soldiers, followed by an assault on a nearby gold-mining site where a village head claims more than 100 miners died, though Reuters could not independently confirm the figure; other reports cite about 23 miners and 8-9 security personnel killed. The attack was reportedly in revenge for miners killing a bandit leader.

events.headline: H5 Avian Influenza Spreads to 695 Wildlife Events Across Australia, Hitting Endangered Sea Lions
events.summary: Australia has recorded 695 confirmed H5 avian influenza events in wildlife since the virus breached the country in June 2026, concentrated in South Australia and Victoria. The outbreak has spilled over into mammals including endangered sea lions and caused mass seabird deaths, though no human infections have been reported.

events.headline: South Korea Recalls Ukraine Ambassador Over Dispute on North Korean POW Transfer
events.summary: South Korea announced Oct 8, 2026 it will recall its ambassador to Ukraine — its first such recall in roughly 18 years — after President Zelenskyy publicly disclosed at the UN General Assembly that Kyiv transferred two North Korean POWs to Seoul, allegedly breaching a bilateral non-disclosure agreement. Seoul is demanding an apology, while Kyiv denies such an agreement existed.

events.headline: US Envoys Pitch New Ukraine Peace Proposals to Kyiv and European Officials in Miami
events.summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Ukrainian officials including Kyrylo Budanov and Rustem Umerov, along with European counterparts, in Miami on Oct 9-10 to discuss new peace proposals. The talks reportedly included a possible partial ceasefire covering energy infrastructure and grain shipments.

events.headline: Student Protests Over Education Funding Spread Across France, Belgium, Italy and Greece
events.summary: Student protests over education budget cuts have spread from France, where more than 6,500 people — mostly minors — have been arrested, to Belgium's Liège (139+ arrests), with school occupations in Turin and Rome and nationwide walkouts called in Greece. The unrest stems from budget deficits exceeding 5% of GDP in France and Belgium.

events.headline: China Sends 19 Military Aircraft Near Taiwan as Lai Vows to 'Deter War' on National Day
events.summary: China sent 19 military aircraft near Taiwan on Oct 9, 2026, with 13 crossing the median line into Taiwan's air defense identification zone, in what Beijing called a 'joint combat-preparedness patrol.' On Taiwan's Oct 10 National Day, President Lai Ching-te held military parades and said increased defense spending aims to deter war amid Chinese pressure.

events.headline: French Bond Yields Hit 24-Year High Amid Record Debt and Political Instability
events.summary: France's 10-year bond yield climbed to nearly 5% — the highest since July 2002 — as public debt reached a record €3.595 trillion, or 119% of GDP, at the end of Q2 2026. The spread between French and German bonds is now the widest since the 2011-2012 eurozone debt crisis.

events.headline: Kosovo Veterans' Protesters Clash With Police Again Over Hague Court Bill
events.summary: War veterans' protesters angered by the September conviction of former president Thaçi and three others gathered outside Kosovo's parliament on Oct 5-6 demanding legislation capping Hague war-crimes court sentences, resulting in three arrests and six injured officers. The amendment still requires committee review before a second reading.

events.headline: Italy's Lower House Passes Meloni-Backed Electoral Reform Dubbed 'Scam Law' by Opposition
events.summary: Italy's Chamber of Deputies approved a sweeping electoral reform, 'Stabilicum,' by a vote of 227-164 on Oct 8, 2026, introducing a proportional system with a majority seat bonus for coalitions winning more than 42% of the vote. The opposition calls it a 'scam law' and plans to challenge its constitutionality.

events.headline: Navi Pillay Awarded 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for Human Rights and International Law Work
events.summary: The Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to Navi Pillay, 85, a South African jurist and former UN High Commissioner for Human Rights and judge at the ICC and ICTR. She is the fifth South African Nobel Peace laureate.

events.headline: UN Report Details Haitian Gang-Politician Ties as Elections Delayed
events.summary: A 94-page UN expert report covering October 2025 to July 2026 names former legislators and officials with ties to Haitian gangs and flags police corruption, arms trafficking and child recruitment. UN rights chief Türk cited at least 5,700 people killed or wounded by gang violence this year, with Haiti indefinitely postponing planned December and February elections.

events.headline: Thai Opposition Files Censure Motion Against PM Anutin, 17 Ministers
events.summary: Thailand's People's Party-led opposition filed a no-confidence motion on Oct 8 under Section 151 against PM Anutin and 17 Bhumjaithai ministers, signed by 145 MPs, alleging 'Blue Regime' influence over institutions, Senate-election manipulation and flood-management failures. Debate is expected in late October.

events.headline: Tens of Thousands Protest Austerity in Brussels, Clash With Riot Police
events.summary: An estimated 30,000 people protested rising living costs and austerity measures in Brussels on Oct 9, 2026, with riot police using tear gas, water cannon and baton charges against groups near Central Station. The demonstration follows earlier unrest in Liège where more than 200 people were arrested.

events.headline: Malaysia Shuts Schools for Over 2 Million Students as Haze From Indonesian Fires Worsens
events.summary: Malaysia closed schools on Oct 9, 2026 in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Johor, Melaka, Negeri Sembilan, Selangor and part of Pahang after haze from Indonesian wildfires pushed the Air Pollutant Index in Kuala Lumpur to about 170. The closures affected more than two million students.

events.headline: Tuareg Separatists Withdraw From Kidal as Mali's Army Retakes City
events.summary: The Azawad Liberation Front announced on Oct 6 a 'controlled withdrawal' from Kidal, which it had held for about six months, citing pressure from Malian airstrikes backed by Russia's Africa Corps. Mali's army subsequently retook the strategic northern city.

events.headline: Bangladesh Records 294 Dengue Deaths in 2026, Fourth-Highest Annual Toll Since 2000
events.summary: Bangladesh has recorded 94,151 dengue cases and 294 deaths for 2026 as of Oct 8, the fourth-highest annual death toll since 2000, with men accounting for 62.3% of infections. The 2026 toll remains far below the 2023 peak of 1,705 deaths.

events.headline: Sudan's Army Chief Burhan Rules Out Talks, Vows to Retake All Land From RSF
events.summary: In an Oct 6 address, Sudanese army chief Burhan said 'there will be no negotiations with the rebels or with any other party,' vowing to continue the campaign until the RSF is eliminated. His statement comes days after a US adviser pushed a 90-day humanitarian ceasefire plan the army wants modified.

events.headline: EU Approves Largest Russia Sanctions Expansion Since 2022, Adding 1,646 Names
events.summary: EU ambassadors approved adding 1,646 names — 743 individuals and 826 entities — to the bloc's Russia sanctions list on Oct 7, 2026, the largest single expansion since the 2022 invasion. Formal adoption by foreign ministers is scheduled for Oct 12 in Luxembourg.

events.headline: PAHO Warns Measles Spread Risk 'Very High' Across Americas Ahead of Mass Gatherings
events.summary: The Pan American Health Organization assessed the risk of measles spread as 'very high' ahead of major religious gatherings, citing 47,459 confirmed cases across the Americas in 2026 — triple the 2025 total and the highest in more than 20 years. The warning builds on PAHO's regional strategy to combat dengue and other arboviral and vaccine-preventable diseases.

events.headline: Myanmar Junta Conducts Three Days of Airstrikes on Villages in Karen State
events.summary: Myanmar's junta carried out three days of airstrikes, Oct 6-8, 2026, using fighter jets and Y-12 aircraft on villages in northern Kawkareik Township, Karen State, dropping more than 50 bombs on Oct 8 alone. The campaign is part of a push to reopen a trade route to Thailand.

events.headline: ISWAP Attacks Nigerian Army Base in Kukawa, Killing 8 Soldiers
events.summary: Islamic State West Africa Province fighters attacked a Nigerian army Special Forces battalion base in Kukawa, Borno State, from four directions on the night of Oct 6, 2026. The army says eight soldiers were killed while more than 25 militants died in the counterattack.

events.headline: Egypt and Ethiopia Expel Diplomats Amid Nile Dam Dispute
events.summary: Ethiopia declared an Egyptian diplomat persona non grata on Oct 1, giving him 48 hours to leave, and Egypt reciprocated by expelling an Ethiopian embassy official. The tit-for-tat move is tied to the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam dispute, intensified after Ethiopia announced plans for three more Blue Nile dams.

events.headline: US Judge Denies House Arrest for Maduro's Wife Cilia Flores
events.summary: A federal judge in the Southern District of New York rejected a defense request on Oct 8 to move Cilia Flores, detained in Brooklyn alongside Nicolás Maduro on US torture charges, to house arrest despite health issues and an offer of GPS monitoring. The judge cited a 'substantial flight risk.'

events.headline: Kenya Opens Dedicated Ebola Screening Gate at Nairobi Airport
events.summary: After Kenya's first imported Ebola case died on Oct 6 following travel from DRC via Uganda, authorities designated Gate 16 at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport for enhanced screening of arrivals from 10 at-risk African countries. No second Kenyan case has been confirmed.

events.headline: Peru Senate Decree-Powers Hearing Erupts Into Shouting Match
events.summary: A Senate Constitutional Commission hearing on Oct 10 over a bill granting President Fujimori's government 90-day decree powers on security and El Niño was disrupted for about 10 minutes by a clash between the interior and justice ministers and opposition Senator Iber Maraví. The debate was suspended until Oct 14.

events.headline: Hungary Suffers Its Most Severe Drought in 126 Years of Records
events.summary: Hungary's 2026 drought is the most severe since records began in 1901, with summer rainfall at just 36% of the 1991-2020 average and Danube water levels at record lows. The drought is straining energy production, water supplies, agriculture and cooling at the Paks nuclear plant.

events.headline: Seventh Arrest Made in Iran-Linked RAF Fairford Security Breach Investigation in UK
events.summary: UK police have made a seventh arrest in the investigation into a Sept 27, 2026 security breach near RAF Fairford, Gloucestershire, which was initially linked to suspected explosives and terror offenses. A 27-year-old British-Iranian dual national was arrested Oct 1 and a 22-year-old British man on Oct 6.

events.headline: Taal Volcano Erupts Briefly With 4,000-Metre Ash Plume
events.summary: A five-minute phreatomagmatic eruption at Taal Volcano on Oct 8 sent an ash plume roughly 4,000 metres high and produced volcanic lightning. PHIVOLCS kept Alert Level 1 in place while 29 families, about 107 people, were evacuated from Agoncillo, Batangas.

events.headline: Poll Shows Rising Support to Stay in Canada Ahead of Alberta Vote
events.summary: A Leger poll in early October found 70% of Albertans want to remain in Canada, up from 65% in August, while 22% support beginning a legal process toward separation. The findings come ahead of Alberta's Oct 19 independence referendum, with 7-10% still undecided.

events.headline: China's Trade Surplus Hits Record Pace, August Figure Reaches $119 Billion
events.summary: China's trade surplus widened to a record pace in 2026, driven by an AI-fueled export surge, with August alone posting a $119.09 billion surplus and a cumulative total of $806 billion for the year. The data underscores China's resilience amid ongoing trade tensions with Western partners.

events.headline: ICE Agent Shoots and Wounds Bronx Man, Sparking NYC Protests
events.summary: A masked ICE agent fired seven rounds during an enforcement operation in the Bronx on Oct 8, striking 28-year-old Oscar Belgal in the neck while his 5-year-old child sat unharmed in the back seat. Belgal survived and is hospitalized in stable condition, while hundreds of protesters demanded video release and an independent investigation.
events.locationName: Marble Hill, Bronx, New York, USA

events.headline: Rare Double Tornado Tears Through Western Sicily, Injures Nine
events.summary: Two waterspouts formed near Marsala on Oct 9 and moved inland as tornadoes, damaging a school complex, overturning vehicles and downing power poles across Marsala, Petrosino and Mazara del Vallo. Nine people suffered minor injuries and no deaths were reported.

events.headline: Fiji Sets Dec 9 Constitutional Referendum Amid Coalition Legal Dispute
events.summary: Fiji's PM Sitiveni Rabuka announced Oct 5, 2026 that a constitutional referendum will be held on Dec 9, with coalition partners and the opposition questioning whether the PM has legal authority to unilaterally set the date. Rabuka maintains his coalition remains intact.

events.headline: Argentina's Dollar-Amnesty Law Takes Effect, Targets Hidden Savings
events.summary: Argentina's 'Inocencia Fiscal II' law, promulgated by President Milei and published in the Official Gazette on Oct 9, lets individuals deposit undeclared 'mattress' dollars, estimated at over $170 billion held outside the banking system, without penalty, while cutting certain tax fines by 25-50%.

events.headline: Venezuela Blackout Protests Spread to Nine States, Block Highways
events.summary: Protests over chronic power cuts, with a deficit of roughly 3,000MW, have spread to at least nine Venezuelan states including Lara, Zulia, Mérida and Aragua, featuring highway blockades such as a 13-hour blockade in Carora. A survey found 62.8% of households now report daily blackouts, up from 37.1% in 2024.

events.headline: Shots Fired at UN Peacekeeping Post Near Israel-Lebanon Border
events.summary: Small-arms fire was directed at a UNIFIL post near Kfar Shouba on the Israel-Lebanon Blue Line on Oct 7, 2026, with no casualties reported. UNIFIL called the incident 'unacceptable' and is investigating, as its Security Council mandate is set to expire Dec 31, 2026.

events.headline: Myanmar Detains Repatriated Rakhine Migrants for Interrogation Over Alleged Arakan Army Ties
events.summary: About 220 Rakhine individuals among 1,476 Myanmar nationals repatriated by sea from Malaysian detention on Sept 29 arrived at Yangon's Thilawa Port on Oct 4, 2026. Rather than being released as the junta claimed, they were taken to a facility in Hlaing Tharyar Township for interrogation over suspected ties to the Arakan Army.

events.headline: Delhi Building Collapse Death Toll Rises to 5 in Seemapuri
events.summary: A four-story building near Idgah Machhli Mandi in Seemapuri, northeast Delhi collapsed on Oct 7, 2026, possibly weakened by cracks from an earlier earthquake in Uttarakhand. The death toll rose to five on Oct 8 after two more bodies, including a pregnant woman and children, were found, with 8-11 survivors rescued.

events.headline: Anak Krakatau Erupts Again With Brief Ash Plume After September's Major Eruption
events.summary: Indonesia's Anak Krakatau volcano erupted again on Oct 9, 2026 at 4:17 p.m. local time, producing an ash plume about 250 meters above the peak that lasted roughly four minutes. The alert level remains at II with a 2km exclusion zone; the eruption is markedly smaller than the major Sept 6 eruption that disrupted thousands of flights.

events.headline: China Resumes October Fuel Exports After Brief Holiday Halt
events.summary: China is resuming October exports of diesel, gasoline and jet fuel, totaling about 3.7 million metric tons, after a brief halt during the Golden Week holiday, according to four trade sources cited by Reuters. Beijing had curbed exports earlier in the year to protect domestic supply amid Middle East disruptions, easing restrictions intermittently since July.

events.headline: Fire Shuts Down Venezuela's Second-Largest Refinery, Cardón, in Falcón State
events.summary: A fire caused by a gas-line rupture forced Venezuela's state oil company PDVSA to halt operations at the 310,000 barrel-per-day Cardón refinery in Punto Fijo on Oct 6, 2026. No injuries were reported, but the shutdown adds pressure to a country already facing a severe energy crisis.

events.headline: Armenia Adds Charges Against Azerbaijani Soldier Who Shot Woman, Children
events.summary: Nasimi Musayev, the Azerbaijani serviceman who illegally crossed into Armenia's Syunik province and shot a woman and her two children, has been held in pretrial detention for two months while prosecutors added illegal border crossing and firearms-smuggling charges, bringing the total to five counts.
